instruction.text: Imagine you have problems in the water. What should you shout?

end.text: That’s right! If you have problems in the water, you should shout for help and wave your arms.

atoms.text: Sandro and Nora are together at an outdoor swimming pool.
While in the water, Nora has been calling for help over and over again, just for fun.
The first time, the lifeguard immediately comes running to help.
The second time, he only looks over at Nora briefly.
The third time, no one cares about her shouting anymore.

instruction.text: Why is it dangerous for Nora to call for help even though everything is fine?

b: ++Because no one will pay attention to Nora if she actually has problems in the water.
Because Nora will be hoarse in the evening.
Because every time Nora calls out, she is rescued from the water.

feedback.end: Exactly! Lifeguards are very hard-working, and we don’t want to waste their time in case there is a real emergency.

instruction.text: Matt is walking along the canal, and he notices that someone has fallen in. Select the item he could throw in to help the person in the water.

feedback.end: This is a life ring. Matt can throw this in to help the person float. If there was no life ring, Matt could throw in anything that floats, such as a football.

b: ++Jump into the canal to rescue the person.
Throw the life ring to the person.

feedback.end: You should never jump in to help someone who is drowning. It is very dangerous because you could also drown.

atoms.a: What two things should Matt do now the person has the life ring?
b: ++Encourage them to kick to get to the edge of the canal.

feedback.end: Someone who has accidentally fallen into the water should always see a paramedic. They could have inhaled water, which is very dangerous even after they get out.

atoms.text: Layla is at the beach on a hot evening. She decides to go for a swim to cool off.
The lifeguards have finished for the day, but she dives into the water anyway.
She swims in the shallow area.
Now, Layla realises she is being pulled out in a rip current. She calls for help, but the lifeguards have gone home.

instruction.text: What should Layla do? Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Layla should swim ((++across away_from)) the beach to the breaking waves, which will push her back to shore. She should stay ((++calm panicked)) to save energy.

text: Rip currents are very fast, so even Olympic swimmers cannot swim against them!

instruction.text: What should Layla have done differently? Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Layla should have waited until ((++the_next_day it_was_dark)), when the lifeguards are back on duty and have put up ((++flags towers)) to show a safe swimming area.
